tasks.title: Configure shared structlog pipeline in main.py with contextvars and JSON renderer

tasks.title: Implement lifespan() async context manager with correct module initialization order
tasks.description: Implement the lifespan() context manager in server/app/main.py following the strict initialization order: AuditLog -> SlangLexicon -> Classifier -> OCR -> TriageRouter -> ContextAgent -> Firebase -> NotificationService. Store all singletons on app.state. Implement graceful shutdown: flush retry queue, close HTTP client, close SQLite. Health check gates: /health returns 'ok' only after all modules initialize.
acceptance_criteria: lifespan() initializes all 8 singletons in the documented order
Startup failure in any module propagates and prevents server from starting
app.state.audit_log, .classifier, .ocr, .triage_router, .context_agent, .notification_service all set after lifespan startup
Graceful shutdown: retry queue drain is called; HTTP clients are closed
/health returns {status: 'ok'} only after lifespan completes successfully

tasks.title: Implement dependencies.py with FastAPI Depends functions for each module
tasks.description: Create server/app/dependencies.py with get_triage_router(), get_notification_service(), get_audit_log(), get_classifier(), get_ocr(), get_context_agent() functions that read from request.app.state. Each function returns the Protocol type (not the concrete class). Wire these into the /classify, /classify-image, /health route handlers.
acceptance_criteria: All 6 Depends functions exist in server/app/dependencies.py
Route handler type annotations use Protocol types (e.g., TriageRouter not TriageRouterImpl)
Test: inject a FakeTriageRouter via app.state.triage_router -> route handler uses the fake
dependencies.py has no circular imports

tasks.title: Implement /classify request handler with full module pipeline
tasks.description: Refactor the /classify endpoint handler in server/app/main.py to use the new module chain: drain retry queue -> classify(text) -> triage.decide() -> if ESCALATE_TO_CA: context_agent.evaluate() -> if alert needed: notification_service.send_alert() -> audit_log.write_audit(). Handle all triage decision paths. Return ClassifyResponse with review_flag when applicable.
acceptance_criteria: SILENT path: returns ClassifyResponse with is_offensive=False, no alert sent
ALERT_DIRECT path: sends alert, returns ClassifyResponse with is_offensive=True
ESCALATE_TO_CA path: calls context_agent.evaluate(), uses AgentResult.is_real_threat for alert decision
REVIEW_NEEDED path: sends alert with review_flag=True in response
audit_log.write_audit() called on every request regardless of outcome

tasks.title: Implement /classify-image request handler with OCR -> classifier pipeline
tasks.description: Refactor the /classify-image endpoint handler in server/app/main.py: extract bytes from multipart -> ocr.extract_text() -> if image_unreadable: return ClassifyImageResponse(image_unreadable=True) -> else: classify(extracted_text) -> same triage/CA/alert pipeline as /classify. Return ClassifyImageResponse with extracted_text field.
acceptance_criteria: POST /classify-image with readable Hebrew screenshot -> ClassifyImageResponse with extracted_text
POST /classify-image with unreadable image -> ClassifyImageResponse(image_unreadable=True)
POST /classify-image > 10MB -> 413 from Gatekeeper (not from the handler)
extracted_text is passed to the same classify/triage/CA pipeline as /classify

tasks.title: Implement /health endpoint with per-module sub-status and liveness/readiness distinction
tasks.description: Implement /health endpoint in server/app/main.py returning HealthResponse with: overall status (ok/degraded), ollama_reachable, audit_log_writable, alerts sub-status (ok/degraded + queued_alerts count). Support ?probe=liveness (always 200) and ?probe=readiness (200 only if classifier reachable). This endpoint is polled by the Android SDK on startup.
acceptance_criteria: GET /health returns {status: 'ok', ollama_reachable: true, audit_log_writable: true, alerts: {status: 'ok'}} when all healthy
GET /health with queued_alerts > 0 returns {alerts: {status: 'degraded', queued_alerts: N}}
GET /health?probe=liveness always returns 200
GET /health?probe=readiness returns 503 when classifier is unreachable
Response time < 500ms (does not block on slow classifier)

tasks.title: Implement SQLiteAuditLog writing to audit.db with 7-day retention
tasks.description: Create server/app/audit_log/sqlite_log.py with SQLiteAuditLog implementing AuditLog Protocol. Create requests and alert_history tables from LLD §5.1 schema. Implement write_audit() for requests table. Implement init() that runs CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS and prunes rows older than 7 days. Non-blocking: write_audit() uses asyncio.to_thread for SQLite calls.
acceptance_criteria: requests table created with all 17 columns and 2 indexes
write_audit() inserts one row per classify request
init() prunes rows where ts < (now - AUDIT_RETENTION_DAYS)
asyncio.to_thread used for all sqlite3 blocking calls
is_writable() returns False if SQLite file is on a read-only filesystem

tasks.title: Implement shared HTTP session pool and register it in lifespan()
tasks.description: Create a single httpx.AsyncClient with limits (max_connections=20, max_keepalive_connections=10) in lifespan() stored as app.state.http_client. OllamaClient and LlmRouter must receive this client as a constructor argument (not create their own). Close the client in lifespan shutdown. This prevents connection pool exhaustion under load.

OllamaClient constructor accepts an httpx.AsyncClient argument
LlmRouter (openai/anthropic) uses the shared client where possible
aclose() called on http_client in lifespan shutdown
Load test: 50 concurrent /classify requests without 'connection pool exhausted' error

tasks.title: Implement server graceful degradation: all module failures return review_needed not 500
tasks.description: Implement the graceful degradation contract from LLD §8: when classifier fails -> REVIEW_NEEDED path (not HTTP 500); when OCR fails -> image_unreadable response; when triage raises -> REVIEW_NEEDED; when CA fails -> frontline-only+review_flag; when FCM fails -> queued. The server NEVER returns 500 to clients for internal module failures that have fallbacks. Implement global exception handler for unhandled exceptions.
acceptance_criteria: Mocked classifier failure -> /classify returns 200 with is_offensive=True, review_flag=True (not 500)
Mocked Tesseract failure -> /classify-image returns 200 with image_unreadable=True
Mocked CA timeout -> /classify returns 200 with review_flag=True in context-aware mode
Mocked FCM failure -> /classify returns 200 (alert queued); /health shows degraded
FastAPI global exception handler catches unhandled exceptions and returns 500 with trace_id

tasks.title: Python dev client at scripts/dev_client.py (HTTP debug tool, no Kotlin toolchain required)
tasks.description: Create scripts/dev_client.py — a Python httpx-based CLI that hits the FastAPI server directly (no SDK dependency). Subcommands: classify, classify-image, health, info, demo, replay. Purpose: quick server-side debugging that does not require running the Kotlin :sdk-cli, useful when iterating on the server during Phase 1–7. Also serves as a reference client for any future TypeScript SDK port. The replay subcommand reads an audit_log trace_id, re-issues the original request, and diffs the new vs historical output (regression test).
acceptance_criteria: python scripts/dev_client.py --help prints subcommands: classify, classify-image, health, info, demo, replay
classify subcommand POSTs to /classify and pretty-prints result with rich.Table
classify-image subcommand uploads multipart form-data and prints extracted_text + classification
demo subcommand runs scripts/golden_inputs.jsonl through the server and prints PASS/FAIL summary (must match Kotlin CLI demo structurally for parity testing)
replay <trace_id> reads server/audit.db via the AuditStore Protocol, finds the row, re-issues the same input, diffs the new vs historical output
All subcommands honor --server URL and --json output flags
Module is importable as a library (from scripts.dev_client import classify) for pytest fixtures

tasks.title: Audit log inspector at scripts/inspect_audit.py (SQLite query + pretty-print)
tasks.description: Create scripts/inspect_audit.py — a SQLite-aware CLI that reads server/audit.db read-only and exposes investigation subcommands. Used during dev to verify the audit_log module is recording correctly, during evaluation prep to slice data for Meeting 8, and during debugging to trace a single request end-to-end. Subcommands: tail (last N classifications), find <trace_id> (full trace including agent_traces + alerts), agent-trace <trace_id> (just the Context Agent reasoning), stats (rollup by triage_decision and label per hour), slice --child_id X --since DATE, export --format csv|jsonl (consumable by Meeting 8 evaluation harness). Read-only — never mutates the DB. Honors AUDIT_DB_PATH env var.
acceptance_criteria: tail -n 10 prints last 10 classifications with all key fields as a rich.Table
find <trace_id> joins classifications + agent_traces + alerts and prints the full audit trail
stats --since YYYY-MM-DD prints a rollup table: triage_decision counts per label per day
export --format jsonl --out X.jsonl produces output consumable by Meeting 8 evaluation scripts
Tool opens audit.db read-only (sqlite3.connect('file:audit.db?mode=ro', uri=True)) — verified by attempted-write smoke test that fails as expected
All subcommands honor AUDIT_DB_PATH env var (default ./audit.db)

tasks.title: Load test script at scripts/load_test.py (NFR validation for Meeting 8)
tasks.description: Create scripts/load_test.py — a locust-or-httpx-based load tester that drives the server with configurable concurrency and traffic mix (text-only, image-only, mixed) and emits a Markdown report. Validates PRD §9 NFR rows: frontline p99 < 100ms, Context Agent p99 < 3s, end-to-end p99 < 5s. Default scenario: 50% non_offensive, 30% borderline, 20% offensive, drawn from scripts/golden_inputs.jsonl. Output: a Markdown report at reports/load_test_YYYY-MM-DD.md with histograms, p50/p95/p99 per endpoint, error rate, and a PASS/FAIL row per NFR target.
acceptance_criteria: python scripts/load_test.py --rps 10 --duration 60s --scenario default produces a Markdown report under reports/
Report includes p50/p95/p99 per endpoint and a histogram
Report has a PASS/FAIL row per NFR: frontline p99 < 100ms, Context Agent p99 < 3s, end-to-end p99 < 5s
--scenario custom.jsonl uses a user-provided traffic mix
Tool reads /metrics during the run to cross-verify server-side p99 vs client-observed p99
Stops early if error rate > 5% over a 30s window (do not waste time on a broken server)
